page.metaDescription: Track supplier catalogs, pricing pages, lead-time changes, and inventory availability across the supply chain. Built for procurement and operations teams.
page.h1: Website monitoring for supply chain and procurement
page.subtitle: Track supplier catalog changes, pricing updates, lead-time shifts, and inventory availability across the supplier network.
page.intro: Procurement and supply-chain teams operate against suppliers whose catalogs and lead times change constantly and rarely come with notification. WebMonitor.fyi tracks supplier pages, distributor catalogs, raw-materials index pages, and freight-tracking portals for the changes that matter — price increases, lead-time extensions, discontinuations, and new product introductions.

challenges.title: Supplier catalog and price visibility
challenges.body: When a supplier silently raises prices or extends lead times by a week, procurement finds out three orders later. Monitoring the catalog page catches it the day it changes.

challenges.title: Multi-supplier comparison
challenges.body: For commodity inputs, watching three or four suppliers in parallel helps procurement time orders and negotiate. One dashboard, multiple supplier monitors.

challenges.title: Discontinuation and EOL tracking
challenges.body: Discontinued parts and end-of-life products show up on supplier pages before the formal notification reaches the buyer. Catching it early means time to qualify a replacement.

challenges.title: Raw-materials index monitoring
challenges.body: Commodity indices (CME, LME, oilprice.com, sector-specific trackers) move daily. Operations teams use the data for forward planning and hedging discussions.

page.limits: WebMonitor tracks public supplier catalogs, distributor product pages, and commodity index pages. Authenticated supplier portals, EDI feeds, contract-specific pricing tiers, and ERP-integrated catalogs all require dedicated integrations rather than a public-page check. Real-time exchange-traded commodity data still needs a dedicated market data feed — public index pages refresh on a slower cadence than the underlying market.

faq.q: Can I monitor a supplier portal that requires login?
faq.a: Login-gated supplier portals are outside the standard product's scope — they require authenticated integrations. Public catalog pages, public price lists, and public product detail pages work directly.

faq.q: Does this work for distributors like McMaster-Carr or Grainger?
faq.a: Yes. Each product page on a public distributor catalog is a monitor URL. Track pricing, availability, and lead time per SKU.
Yes. Public commodity index pages (oilprice.com, kitco.com for metals, freight indices) work as monitor sources. For real-time exchange data, dedicated market data feeds are still required.

faq.q: How many monitors does a typical procurement team run?
faq.a: Small teams: 30–60 covering primary suppliers. Mid-size: 150–400 covering supplier network plus commodity indices. The dashboard handles bulk monitor management at any scale.
